name: Sprint and kanabn column must height
description:
1. The issue: Sprint and Kanban board columns grew beyond their parent's height, pushing cards out of reach instead of scrolling internally.
2. Root cause: column wrappers were content-sized (`self-start`) and the Kanban grid lacked a definite height, so the `max-h-full`/`h-full` caps never resolved against the parent.
3. Fix: bound the columns to the parent height (`h-full`/`auto-rows-fr`) and let the inner task list be the only scrolling region.
4. Two files changed: `SprintBoardCanvas.vue` (wrapper `self-start` → `h-full`) and `KanbanColumnView.vue` (root/column/tasks sizing and overflow).
5. Result: columns now cap to the board area and scroll, keeping every card accessible.

messages.content:
Sprint and Kanban columns max height is the parents max height then scroll.
Now the column growths too much and can't access the cards. Fix it

I'll analyze the situation first by examining the relevant files. ``` Read 2 file(s) | Successfully read: src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardColumn.vue, src/components/kanban/KanbanColumnView.vue ``` Let me look at how these views are used in the parent components to understand the height context. ``` Search completed: 4 queries executed, 40 documents found ``` Let me examine the grid view and how the board canvas is used. ``` Read 2 file(s) | Successfully read: src/components/kanban/KanbanGridView.vue, src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardView.vue | Failed to read 1 file(s): src/components/kanban/KanbanBoardView.vue ``` ``` Search completed: 2 queries executed, 20 documents found ``` Let me find where `KanbanColumnView` is actually used to understand both board contexts. ``` Search completed: 5 queries executed, 50 documents found ``` ## 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking **Core Requirement:** Make Sprint and Kanban columns cap their height to the parent container's height and scroll internally, instead of growing unbounded and hiding cards (which become unreachable). **Root cause:** - **SprintBoardCanvas.vue** — the column wrapper uses `self-start`, which overrides the flex row's default `stretch`. The wrapper therefore shrinks to its *content* height. The inner `SprintBoardColumn` has `max-h-full`, but that resolves against the wrapper (which is content-sized) → the cap is meaningless, so the column grows past the canvas. Because the canvas has `overflow-y-hidden`, the overflowed cards get clipped and can't be reached. - **KanbanColumnView.vue** — the draggable root is `grid ... min-h-60 overflow-x-scroll` with no definite height, so rows auto-size to content and the columns' `h-full` grows with them; the whole thing overflows and cards become inaccessible. **Fix strategy:** Give the column wrapper/container a definite height bound to the parent (`h-full`), and let the existing inner `overflow-y-auto flex-1 min-h-0` task list do the scrolling. **Target files:** | File | Action | | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardCanvas.vue` | Modify | | `src/components/kanban/KanbanColumnView.vue` | Modify | ## 2. Minimum Changes Approach 1. **SprintBoardCanvas.vue**: column wrapper `self-start` → `h-full` so the column's `max-h-full` resolves against the parent height and the task list scrolls. 2. **KanbanColumnView.vue**: bound the root to parent height (`h-full min-h-0`), size the implicit grid row to fill it (`auto-rows-fr`), stop the whole column from scrolling (`overflow-hidden` instead of `overflow-auto`), and let the task list scroll (`min-h-0`). Also pin the header (`shrink-0`). ## 3. File changes ```vue src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardCanvas.vue ``` ```vue src/components/kanban/KanbanColumnView.vue ``` ## 4. File Change Summary Tables | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardCanvas.vue` | Modify | column wrapper `div` | `self-start` → `h-full` so the column wrapper fills the parent row height. This makes `SprintBoardColumn`'s existing `max-h-full` resolve against the real available height, capping the column and letting its `overflow-y-auto flex-1 min-h-0` task list scroll instead of overflowing past the canvas. | | `src/components/kanban/KanbanColumnView.vue` | Modify | root `` `class` | `min-h-60 grid grid-flow-col overflow-x-scroll` → `h-full min-h-0 grid grid-flow-col auto-rows-fr overflow-x-auto overflow-y-hidden`, bounding the board to the parent height and sizing the single grid row to fill it (`auto-rows-fr`). | | `src/components/kanban/KanbanColumnView.vue` | Modify | column `div` `class` | `overflow-auto h-full flex flex-col` → `overflow-hidden h-full flex flex-col min-h-0`. The whole column no longer scrolls (which pushed the header away); only the task list scrolls. `min-h-0` allows the flex child to shrink. | | `src/components/kanban/KanbanColumnView.vue` | Modify | column header `div` `class` | Added `shrink-0` so the header keeps its size and isn't squished when the task list is constrained. | | `src/components/kanban/KanbanColumnView.vue` | Modify | tasks wrapper `div` `class` | Added `min-h-0` to `column-tasks grow overflow-y-auto` so it becomes the scrolling region within the capped column. |
